artiest/stile-antico.text:
Stile Antico is a British vocal ensemble that specialises in polyphonic early music from before the eighteenth century. Like groups such as The Tallis Scholars and The Sixteen, it grew out of the choral tradition of the Oxford and Cambridge colleges. Unusually, the ensemble has no conductor: the twelve singers rehearse and perform as chamber musicians, an approach praised by critics. The group was founded in 2001 and in 2005 won the audience prize at the Early Music Network Young Artists' Competition.

The debut album Music for Compline from 2007 became a great success after it was featured on NPR, and reached number two on the Billboard Classical chart. It received the Diapason d'or of the year and a Grammy nomination. Song of Songs from 2009 won the Gramophone Award for early music and spent three weeks at the top of the Billboard Classical chart. The Golden Renaissance: Josquin des Prez won the first Gramophone Award for Spatial Audio in 2021. The group has recorded fifteen albums for Harmonia Mundi, and in 2020 it announced a collaboration with Decca Classics. In 2018 it performed at the Grammy Awards ceremony.

Stile Antico has collaborated widely with others, including Fretwork, B'Rock and Sting, with whom it toured Europe, Australia and the Far East with Songs from the Labyrinth, based on the music of John Dowland, and guested on his album If on a Winter's Night.... In this way the ensemble brought Renaissance polyphony to a wide audience.
artiest/stile-antico.listen: Listen to a motet by Josquin des Prez on The Golden Renaissance: Josquin des Prez. Notice how the voices take up the same melody in turn, without a conductor.

artiest/sting.text:
Sting's real name is Gordon Sumner, and he was born on 2 October 1951 in Wallsend, by the shipyards of north-east England. He learned to play bass by playing records at a faster speed, so that he could hear the bass lines better. After training as a teacher he stood in front of a class for two years and played jazz in the evenings. He got his nickname in a jazz band, because in his black-and-yellow striped jumper he looked like a wasp.

In 1977 he formed The Police with Stewart Copeland and Andy Summers, in which he sang, played bass and wrote most of the songs. The band began with a punk-like sound, but found its own voice in a mix of reggae and bare, tight rock. Roxanne and Every Breath You Take became their best-known songs, and Synchronicity (1983) was their last album. In 1985 Sting started his solo career with The Dream of the Blue Turtles, recorded with jazz musicians such as the saxophonist Branford Marsalis. It included If You Love Somebody Set Them Free and Russians. Later came, among others, ...Nothing Like the Sun (1987), with Englishman in New York, and Ten Summoner's Tales (1993), with Fields of Gold.

As a solo artist Sting mixes rock with jazz, reggae, classical music and world music. In 1985 he appeared at Live Aid and sang along on Money for Nothing by Dire Straits. With The Police he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2003.
artiest/sting.listen: Listen to Russians (1985). Notice the melody, which Sting borrowed from the Lieutenant Kijé suite by the Russian composer Prokofiev, and how the sombre, restrained sound suits the fear of nuclear war.

artiest/stochelo-rosenberg.text: Stochelo Rosenberg was born in Helmond into a Sinti family and learned to play guitar by copying records by Django Reinhardt. With his cousins Nous'che and Nonnie Rosenberg he formed the Rosenberg Trio, which made its debut in 1989 with Seresta. He plays fast and melodically, with the typical technique of gypsy jazz. The trio performed in the Netherlands and abroad, including at the North Sea Jazz Festival. In 2017 he played the guitar parts for the French film Django, about Reinhardt. Rosenberg is regarded as one of the best guitarists in his tradition.
artiest/stochelo-rosenberg.listen: Hear the fast, clear solo guitar above the pumping rhythm guitar.

artiest/stock-aitken-waterman.text:
Stock Aitken Waterman was an English writing and production trio consisting of Mike Stock, Matt Aitken and Pete Waterman. In January 1984 Stock and Aitken sought out the DJ Waterman in London, and that same year they made their first records. These caught on in gay clubs and discos, where the fast dance music was called Hi-NRG. In March 1985 they scored their first British number 1 with You Spin Me Round (Like a Record) by Dead or Alive.

In 1985 they built a studio of their own in London, which soon came to be called the Hit Factory. One hit followed another there: Venus by Bananarama, Respectable by Mel and Kim and, in 1987, Never Gonna Give You Up by Rick Astley, perhaps their greatest success. That same year Waterman started his own label PWL. One of the first artists was the Australian soap star Kylie Minogue. Stock and Aitken wrote and recorded I Should Be So Lucky with her in forty minutes, and it became a number 1 in 1988. Her colleague Jason Donovan also had hits with the trio.

The formula combined the beat of Hi-NRG with romantic lyrics in the Motown tradition and melodies from Italo disco. In the years 1984 to 1989 that style was called Eurobeat. The trio scored more than a hundred hits in the British top 40 and thirteen number 1s. For a long time critics regarded it as conveyor-belt work, but their music has since been judged more and more positively.
artiest/stock-aitken-waterman.listen: Listen to Never Gonna Give You Up by Rick Astley (1987). Notice the tight drum machine and the continuous synthesizer bass, and how Astley's warm, low voice rises above them.

artiest/stormzy.text:
Stormzy, real name Michael Ebenezer Kwadjo Omari Owuo Jr, is a British rapper, singer and songwriter. He was born in 1993 in Thornton Heath, a suburb of Croydon in south London, to a Ghanaian mother, and grew up in South Norwood. He started rapping at eleven and took on older rappers at his youth centre. Before his breakthrough he worked for two years in quality control at an oil refinery in Southampton.

In 2012 he made his mark on the British underground scene with his series of freestyles Wicked Skengman over classic grime beats. In 2014 he released the EP Dreamers Disease himself and won the MOBO Award for best grime act, which he won again in 2015. His freestyle Shut Up, recorded over an instrumental by XTC, reached the British top ten in 2015, after a campaign for the Christmas number 1. The debut album Gang Signs & Prayer from 2017 was the first grime album to top the British album chart and won a Brit Award. In 2019 he got his first number 1 with Vossi Bop and was the first British rapper to headline Glastonbury, wearing a stab-proof vest designed by Banksy. Heavy Is the Head in 2019 and This Is What I Mean in 2022 followed.

His music combines the hard, fast style of grime with singing and gospel-like moments. He showed that grime, a style from the streets of London, could reach a large audience.
artiest/stormzy.listen: Listen to Shut Up. Notice how little there is beneath the voice: a bare, hard beat and a rap that rolls on at high speed.

artiest/stratos-pagioumtzis.text:
Stratos Pagioumtzis was a Greek rebetiko singer, also known as Stratos the Lazy or simply Stratos. He was born in 1904 in Ayvalik in Asia Minor and left for Greece for the Greco-Turkish War of 1919 to 1922. He settled in the port city of Piraeus and made a living as a fisherman and later as a ship's provisioner. Still, he dreamed of earning his money from music. At the end of the 1920s he began singing professionally and in 1933 his first recordings appeared.

In 1934 he formed the quartet I Tetras i Xakousti tou Peiraios, the famous four of Piraeus, with the rebetiko singers Yiorgos Batis, Anestis Delias and Markos Vamvakaris. In 1937, under the dictatorial regime of Metaxas, he was convicted of drug use and exiled to the Cycladic island of Sifnos. He recorded more than four hundred songs and worked with composers such as Vassilis Tsitsanis, Giannis Papaioannou, Bayianteras and Panagiotis Toundas.

The beauty of his voice made him famous. He is regarded as one of the greatest singers of the classic rebetiko era. Tsitsanis said that Pagioumtzis had nightingales in his throat. Rebetiko is the urban music of the Greek port districts and of refugees from Asia Minor, often with the bouzouki. Pagioumtzis died in 1971 in New York of a stroke, after a concert in a Greek nightclub.
artiest/stratos-pagioumtzis.listen: Listen to a recording by Stratos Pagioumtzis from the 1930s or 1940s, for example Τα τσαγκαράκια. Notice the warm, clear voice and the sharp sound of the bouzouki beneath it.

artiest/stuart-sutcliffe.text:
Stuart Sutcliffe was a British painter and the first bass player of the Beatles. He was born in Edinburgh in 1940 and grew up in Liverpool. At the Liverpool College of Art he met John Lennon, through a mutual friend, Bill Harry. Sutcliffe was regarded as one of the stars of the school, and he helped Lennon with his coursework for examinations. In early 1960 Lennon moved in with him in the attic flat at Gambier Terrace.

Lennon and Paul McCartney persuaded Sutcliffe to buy a Höfner bass guitar. He did not have much experience: he had had piano lessons and had played a little guitar. In May 1960 he joined Lennon, McCartney and George Harrison, who were then performing as the Silver Beatles. Together with Lennon he came up with the band name, inspired by Buddy Holly's Crickets and by a double meaning of the word. In Hamburg the group played long nights in clubs such as the Kaiserkeller. There Sutcliffe met the photographer Astrid Kirchherr, to whom he became engaged.

In July 1961 he left the band to paint. He studied at the art academy in Hamburg with Eduardo Paolozzi, who called him one of his best students. His work was in line with Abstract Expressionism. Sutcliffe suffered from severe headaches and died in April 1962 of a cerebral haemorrhage, before the Beatles became famous. For that reason he is sometimes called the fifth Beatle. His influence lay above all in the early years: in his style, in his friendship with Lennon and in the band he helped to name.
artiest/stuart-sutcliffe.listen: Listen to Love Me Do by the Beatles and notice the bass line. It was played by McCartney, who took over the bass when Sutcliffe had left the group.

artiest/su-tenore-de-ollolai.text:
Su Tenore de Ollolai is a vocal group from Ollolai, a village in Sardinia. The island lies in the Mediterranean, west of the Italian mainland and south of Corsica. It has its own language, Sardinian, which is protected alongside Italian. Because of this location and the mountainous interior, old customs were preserved in Sardinia, in music too. The group sings in the tradition of polyphonic male singing, which in Sardinian is called cantu a tenore.

In the course the group features with Arvure Ch'est Fozida, recorded in 1981. It is an example of music without instruments, in which everything revolves around voices that together form a single sound. Such singing is not pop music in the ordinary sense. It belongs to the community in which it is sung, to festivities and to the village itself, and not to the hit parades.

Precisely for that reason it is important for anyone who wants to understand the history of pop music. It shows that rhythm, harmony and group singing are far older than the studio and the electric guitar. Anyone who later listens to world music, or to pop musicians who sought their inspiration far outside America and England, sooner or later meets sounds from such traditions. The 1981 recording makes that audible without words.
artiest/su-tenore-de-ollolai.listen: Listen to Arvure Ch'est Fozida and notice how the voices together form a single sound. Can you hear one voice leading, and how do the other voices respond?

artiest/suicidal-tendencies.text:
Suicidal Tendencies is an American hardcore punk and crossover thrash band, founded in 1980 in Venice, Los Angeles, by the singer Mike Muir. Muir is the only member who has always been part of it. At first he saw the group as a party band, but it soon became the centre of his life. The early years were bumpy: in 1982 the magazine Flipside chose them as the worst band, and a year later as the best new band.

The debut album Suicidal Tendencies from 1983 brought the single Institutionalized, one of the first hardcore punk videos to get heavy play on MTV. Join the Army from 1987 was the first album on the Billboard 200 and showed a heavier sound that helped to shape crossover thrash. At Epic Records came How Will I Laugh Tomorrow When I Can't Even Smile Today, Controlled by Hatred/Feel Like Shit... Déjà Vu and Lights... Camera... Revolution!, the last two gold. The Art of Rebellion from 1992 was their greatest success, with Asleep at the Wheel, Nobody Hears and I'll Hate You Better. In those years the band broadened its sound, from thrash metal to progressive music and funk. Still Cyco After All These Years and Suicidal for Life followed.

In 1995 the group stopped, but Muir re-formed it a year later with Mike Clark. Albums followed such as Freedumb and Free Your Soul and Save My Mind, and later 13 from 2013 and World Gone Mad from 2016. Together with D.R.I., Corrosion of Conformity and Stormtroopers of Death, Suicidal Tendencies is regarded as one of the fathers of crossover thrash. Musicians who played in it include the bass players Robert Trujillo and Stephen Thundercat Bruner.
artiest/suicidal-tendencies.listen: Listen to Institutionalized. Notice how Muir tells the story as the monologue of a discontented teenager, over a tight, fast accompaniment that keeps getting harder.

artiest/sukhwinder-singh.text:
Sukhwinder Singh is an Indian playback singer, composer, lyricist and producer who works mainly for Hindi films. He was born in 1971 in Amritsar, Punjab, into a Sikh family. As a young man he did athletics and sprinting, before music began to interest him more. He took music lessons from the Punjabi musician B. S. Narang and began a music career at seventeen. After that he released the Punjabi album Munda Southhall Da, together with T. Singh.

The composer duo Laxmikant-Pyarelal noticed him. In the late 1980s and early 1990s he worked for them as a musical arranger and sang in choruses and in short fragments of songs. One of his first recordings was Chitti Aayi Hai from the film Naam in 1986. His first solo came with Aaja Sanam in the film Khilaaf in 1991. In 1997 he made his debut in a Tamil film with Lucky Lucky from Ratchagan, composed by A. R. Rahman. His great breakthrough followed with Chaiyya Chaiyya from Dil Se.. in 1998, also by Rahman, for which he received a Filmfare Award. He also sang in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Punjabi, Marathi, Urdu and Bengali.

In 2008 he was among the singers of Jai Ho from Slumdog Millionaire, the song that received an Oscar and a Grammy. His second Filmfare Award was for Haule Haule from Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, and for Bismil from Haider he received the National Film Award for best male playback singer in 2014. In this way he is one of the best-known voices of Indian film music, and he brought the sound of Bollywood to a worldwide audience.
artiest/sukhwinder-singh.listen: Listen to Chaiyya Chaiyya. Notice the powerful, full voice of the singer and how the rhythm of the drums pulls you along, as if you were on a moving train.

artiest/sun-ra.text: Herman Blount from Birmingham, Alabama, played piano in the orchestra of Fletcher Henderson, his great example, in 1946 and 1947. In Chicago he took the name Sun Ra and said that he came from Saturn. With his big band, the Arkestra, he lived together as a commune. The band played swing, bebop, free improvisation and early electronic sounds on organ and synthesizer, in costumes from ancient Egypt and space travel. Sun Ra released his records on a label of his own, El Saturn. In 1972 he made the film Space Is the Place. His ideas about space and Black history later came to be called Afrofuturism.
artiest/sun-ra.listen: Hear how a swinging big band and strange electronic sounds go together.

artiest/sun-ra-arkestra.text:
The Sun Ra Arkestra is an American jazz group that arose in the mid-1950s as the ensemble accompanying the keyboard player and composer Sun Ra. Sun Ra led the group until his death in 1993. He and the orchestra are regarded as pioneers of Afrofuturism. The group has its headquarters in a row house in the Germantown district of Philadelphia. The saxophonist Marshall Allen, a member since 1958, has lived and worked there since 1968 and has led the orchestra since 1995, after John Gilmore. There are usually more than twelve members.

The Arkestra draws on swing, rock 'n' roll, Chicago blues, improvisation and electronics. The musicians perform in colourful costumes with capes and headdresses, in an Afrofuturist style. The singer June Tyson, who joined in 1968, shaped the sound with her singing and spoken word and contributed to the costumes and choreography. The long list of albums includes Super-Sonic Jazz from 1957, Jazz in Silhouette from 1958, Art Forms of Dimensions Tomorrow from 1965, The Magic City from 1966 and Atlantis from 1969.

After Sun Ra's death Allen released new albums again under the name Sun Ra Arkestra, beginning with A Song for the Sun in 1999. In 2017 the group was the opening act for Solange. The album Swirling from 2020 contains the first studio recording of Sun Ra's Darkness. Lights on a Satellite from 2024 received a Grammy nomination in 2026 for best large jazz ensemble album. In 2009 the Institute of Contemporary Art in Philadelphia devoted an exhibition to the group.
artiest/sun-ra-arkestra.listen: Listen to a recording from the 1960s, for example from The Magic City. Notice the changing, sometimes rough sounds of saxophones and percussion, and how a composition suddenly turns into free improvisation.

artiest/sunny-murray.text:
Sunny Murray was born in 1936 in Idabel, Oklahoma, and grew up with an uncle. He began drumming at the age of nine. After a childhood in Philadelphia he moved to New York in 1956, where he played with, among others, Red Allen, Ted Curson and Jackie McLean. He was one of the pioneers of free jazz drumming.

The turning point came in 1959, when he first played with the pianist Cecil Taylor. Together with Taylor and the saxophonist Jimmy Lyons he made a stylistic breakthrough in Scandinavia in 1962, captured on Nefertiti the Beautiful One Has Come. There he also met the saxophonist Albert Ayler. Murray played in Ayler's trio with the bass player Gary Peacock and recorded, among other things, Spiritual Unity with him. Under his own name he made his debut in 1965 with Sonny's Time Now, released on Leroi Jones's label. Later he lived in Europe, where he made records for BYG Actuel. In 1980 he played with Taylor again, on It Is in the Brewing Luminous. He died in 2017.

Murray gave up the drummer's role as timekeeper and played mainly texture: a sustained hailstorm of strokes, with continuous shimmering on the rims of the cymbals, an irregular stream on the snare and scattered accents on the bass drum. In this way he freed the soloist from the beat. For the development of free jazz that was essential: he let Ayler and Taylor move wherever they wanted.
artiest/sunny-murray.listen: Listen to Spiritual Unity by Albert Ayler and notice how Murray does not play a fixed pulse, but lays a rolling bed of cymbals and snare beneath the saxophone.

artiest/survivor.text:
Survivor was an American rock band, formed in Chicago in 1978 by Jim Peterik and Frankie Sullivan. Peterik had previously played in The Ides of March and found the band name in a lyric on the sleeve of his own solo album. The singer Dave Bickler, who also worked as a jingle writer in Chicago, completed the first line-up. The album Survivor came out at the end of 1979 on the Scotti Bros. label and did not yet produce a big hit.

With Premonition (1981) the band got going better, with Poor Man's Son as its first hit in the American Top 40. The breakthrough followed in 1982, when Sylvester Stallone asked the band to make the title song for the film Rocky III. That became Eye of the Tiger, which spent six weeks at number one in the United States. The album of the same name came out that same year. After Caught in the Game (1983), Bickler left the band because of a voice problem, and Jimi Jamison took his place. With him came Vital Signs (1984) and When Seconds Count (1986), with hits such as High on You and The Search Is Over. In 1988 the band went on hiatus. Later Survivor returned in changing line-ups, and in 2006 Reach appeared.

The music is melodic, polished arena rock with guitars, synthesizers and vocals that are easy to sing along to. Survivor became a model of the American radio rock sound of the 1980s, and Eye of the Tiger remained a fixture in sport and film.
artiest/survivor.listen: Listen to Eye of the Tiger and notice the short guitar motif it begins with and how the drums and the vocals build the tension towards the chorus.

artiest/susan-ann-sulley.text:
Susan Ann Sulley is an English singer, born in 1963 in Sheffield. She is one of the two female singers of the synth-pop band The Human League. Together with her school friend Joanne Catherall she was spotted in 1980, at the age of seventeen, by the singer Philip Oakey in the Sheffield club Crazy Daisy. The band had just split up and had to go on a European tour within a week. Oakey asked the two girls along as dancers and singers, even though they had no experience at all. The audience, which had expected the original all-male band, received them at first with hostility.

During that tour Oakey had them sing along on existing songs and was happy with the result. In 1981 the album Dare came out, and Sulley sang on Don't You Want Me, a duet about a singer who leaves her bossy discoverer. In the accompanying video she herself played the lead role, in a trench coat on a wet winter night. The song reached number one in the United Kingdom and the United States. Hysteria (1984) followed, and the single Human, which reached number one in the United States. After a lean period the group returned in 1994 with Tell Me When and the album Octopus, on which Sulley sang the ballad One Man in My Heart.

Sulley shows how a pop act could broaden its sound: the cool synthesizers gained a human, direct voice. The group is still touring.
artiest/susan-ann-sulley.listen: Listen to Don't You Want Me and notice how the voice of Philip Oakey and that of Sulley sound like two sides of the same quarrel, above a tight synthesizer pattern.

artiest/susan-graham.text:
Susan Graham is an American mezzo-soprano, born in 1960 in Roswell, New Mexico, and raised in West Texas. She began as a pianist and sang in the church choir from an early age. After studying at Texas Tech University and the Manhattan School of Music she made her debut in 1985 at the Eugene Opera as Hänsel in Hansel und Gretel. In 1988 she was one of the winners of the Metropolitan Opera National Council Auditions.

In her first years she became known in trouser roles, boys' parts sung by women, such as Cherubino in Le nozze di Figaro, the Composer in Ariadne auf Naxos and Octavian in Der Rosenkavalier. Later she sang leading roles at, among others, the Metropolitan Opera, the Royal Opera House, La Scala, the Opéra de Paris and the Vienna State Opera. She took part in world premieres of contemporary operas, including Dead Man Walking by Jake Heggie, in which she sang Sister Helen Prejean. In 2004 she won a Grammy Award for best classical vocal performance.

Graham is known as an advocate of French song. Her recordings include Berlioz, Ravel and Britten alongside Songs of Ned Rorem and La Belle Époque: The Songs of Reynaldo Hahn. Her voice has a warm, dark colour and a clear, natural articulation, so that both the great opera roles and the intimate songs are shown to good advantage. She shows how classical repertoire can stay close to the word and the story.
artiest/susan-graham.listen: Listen to a recording of Les Nuits d’été and notice how Graham sings Berlioz's long melodic lines, with great attention to the pronunciation of the French.

artiest/suzanne-vega.text:
Suzanne Vega is an American singer-songwriter, born in 1959 in Santa Monica and raised in New York. She studied English literature at Barnard College and performed in small venues in Greenwich Village, in the circle around the Fast Folk songwriters. In 1984 she got a contract with a major label, as one of the first Fast Folk artists. Her debut album Suzanne Vega came out in 1985 on A&M with, among others, Marlene on the Wall. She also wrote the lyrics and sang on two songs of Songs from Liquid Days by Philip Glass.

The breakthrough came with Solitude Standing (1987) and the single Luka, which is about an abused child. Years later Vega said that the song also referred to her own experiences. In 1989 she was the first woman to headline Glastonbury. The a cappella song Tom's Diner from that same album was remixed into a dance track in 1990 by the British production duo DNA and became her biggest hit. Later albums are Days of Open Hand (1990), 99.9 F° (1992) and Nine Objects of Desire (1996). In 2025 Flying with Angels came out.

The music is folk-oriented and sounds light and precise, with acoustic guitar and a cool, almost spoken style of singing. Her recording of Tom's Diner was used as a test in the development of the MP3 format, which earned her the nickname Mother of the MP3.
artiest/suzanne-vega.listen: Listen to Tom's Diner and notice how her voice sounds without accompaniment: almost spoken, with a quietly told story about an ordinary morning in a café.

artiest/sven-ake-johansson.text:
Sven-Åke Johansson was a Swedish drummer, composer, poet, writer and visual artist, born in 1943 in Mariestad. He began in dance bands and then played, among others, in ensembles around Bobo Stenson. From 1968 he lived in Berlin. There he became one of the first European free jazz drummers, as a member of the trio of the saxophonist Peter Brötzmann with the bass player Peter Kowald. That group recorded For Adolphe Sax (1967) and Machine Gun (1968). He also played in the Globe Unity Orchestra and briefly in an early form of Tangerine Dream.

In 1972 Schlingerland came out, one of the first solo records by a free jazz drummer. From 1976 he formed a long-running duo with the pianist Alexander von Schlippenbach, in which he also played accordion and recited spontaneous poems. He used unusual materials for percussion, such as foam rubber and telephone directories, and wrote pieces of his own, including Konzert für 12 Traktoren. From 2010 he worked with the singer and composer Oliver Augst on the programme Eisler im Sitzen, and later also with Jan Jelinek on modular synthesizer. He made almost forty records and wrote volumes of poetry and radio plays. He died in 2025.

Johansson shows that European free jazz left more room for humour, sound exploration and visual art than its American example. His work runs from wild improvisation to slow, almost theatrical sound plays, and made him a distinctive voice in the Berlin scene.
artiest/sven-ake-johansson.listen: Listen to Schlingerland and notice how, with only drums and percussion, he builds a whole piece, without melody or fixed metre.

artiest/sven-vath.text:
Sven Väth is a German DJ and producer, born in 1964. He grew up near Frankfurt, in a family that ran a café with a small dance floor. In the summer of 1980 he travelled to Ibiza and decided there to become a DJ. In 1982 he was resident DJ at the club Dorian Gray in Frankfurt, where he met Michael Münzing and Luca Anzilotti. With them he formed Off, which had a European hit in 1986 with Electrica Salsa. Väth was twenty-two at the time and briefly became a pop star. Münzing and Anzilotti went on to Snap!.

In 1988 Väth opened the club Omen in Frankfurt, which is regarded as one of the cradles of German techno. With his own labels Eye Q and Harthouse Records he released Accident in Paradise (1992) and The Harlequin, the Robot and the Ballet-Dancer (1994). After that he signed to Virgin, for Fusion (1998), Contact (2000) and Fire (2002). In 1996 he started Cocoon: first parties, later a booking agency and record label. His Monday nights at Amnesia on Ibiza kept the island's underground sound alive, at a time when trance and commercial music dominated. In 2022 Catharsis came out.

Väth plays vinyl, with two turntables and a mixer, and sometimes plays long sets lasting many hours. His music runs from techno and trance to electro, and he is one of the best-known faces of German club culture.
artiest/sven-vath.listen: Listen to Electrica Salsa by Off and notice the tight electronic groove, which you can hear as a forerunner of German club music.

artiest/sweet.text:
The Sweet, also simply Sweet, is a British glam rock band that broke through in the 1970s. The best-known line-up consisted of the singer Brian Connolly, bass player Steve Priest, guitarist Andy Scott and drummer Mick Tucker. The group came together in 1968 in London, at first under the name The Sweetshop. Its roots lie in the soul band Wainwright's Gentlemen from the early 1960s.

The first big success came in 1971 with Funny, Funny, which they made with the songwriters Nicky Chinn and Mike Chapman and the producer Phil Wainman. Co-Co, Block Buster! and Hell Raiser followed, and in 1973 The Ballroom Blitz. Teenage Rampage in 1974 and Fox on the Run in 1975 were also hits. In the United Kingdom the group had thirteen songs in the top twenty. In the United States, Little Willy, The Ballroom Blitz, Fox on the Run and Love Is Like Oxygen reached the top ten. The group's albums included Funny How Sweet Co-Co Can Be from 1971, Desolation Boulevard and Sweet Fanny Adams from 1974, Give Us a Wink in 1976 and Level Headed in 1977. In 1979 Connolly left for a solo career, and in 1981 the group ceased to exist.

The music developed from the bubblegum of Funny, Funny, which resembled the Archies, to a harder sound influenced by The Who, with high backing vocals. Sweet shows how glam rock combined light pop melodies with hard guitars. That is why it returns in the chapter on the 1970s.
artiest/sweet.listen: Listen to The Ballroom Blitz and notice the high backing vocals and the driving drums. Can you hear how the singer adds remarks in between, and how the song builds in tempo and power?

artiest/swf-sinfonieorchester.text:
The SWF-Sinfonieorchester was the symphony orchestra of the south-west German broadcaster Südwestfunk, based in Baden-Baden. The orchestra began in 1946, at first with members of the town's disbanded spa orchestra. When that spa orchestra was revived two years later, the radio orchestra was reconstituted. Hans Rosbaud became the first chief conductor. He was known as an advocate of modern music, and the music director Heinrich Strobel also set great store by contemporary composers. As a result the orchestra's emphasis lay on new music.

After Rosbaud (1948 to 1962) the orchestra was led by, among others, Ernest Bour, Kazimierz Kord, Michael Gielen and Sylvain Cambreling. In 1998 Südwestfunk merged into Südwestrundfunk, which took over the orchestra. The orchestra made commercial recordings for the Hänssler label, including music by Messiaen, Bartók, Stravinsky, Schoenberg and Wolfgang Rihm. In 2012 the broadcaster decided on a merger with the Stuttgart radio orchestra. The orchestra gave its last concert in Freiburg in 2016, under François-Xavier Roth. The new orchestra is called the SWR Symphonieorchester.

One of the most widely heard recordings by this orchestra is Atmospheres by György Ligeti, conducted by Ernest Bour, which is on the soundtrack of 2001: A Space Odyssey. In this way avant-garde orchestral music reached a large audience outside the concert hall.
artiest/swf-sinfonieorchester.listen: Listen to Atmospheres by Ligeti, as heard in 2001: A Space Odyssey, and notice how there is no melody or rhythm, only slowly moving blocks of orchestral sound.

artiest/swf-sinfonieorchester-baden-bade.text:
The SWF Sinfonieorchester Baden-Baden was a German radio orchestra, attached to the broadcaster Südwestfunk in Baden-Baden. It came into being in 1946, with members of the town's spa orchestra as its core. Two years later that spa orchestra was restarted, which gave the radio orchestra a new set-up. Hans Rosbaud, who was known as a champion of modern music, became the first chief conductor. Together with the music director Heinrich Strobel he opted for a programme with a great deal of contemporary music.

Later, Ernest Bour, Michael Gielen and Sylvain Cambreling, among others, followed as chief conductor. After the merger of the broadcasters in 1998 the orchestra came under Südwestrundfunk. The orchestra recorded for Hänssler, with works by Messiaen, Bartók, Stravinsky, Schoenberg and Wolfgang Rihm. In 2016 it ceased to exist, after being merged with the radio orchestra of Stuttgart into the SWR Symphonieorchester. The last concert, in Freiburg, was conducted by François-Xavier Roth.

The orchestra became widely known through the recording of Atmospheres by Ligeti under Ernest Bour, which is used in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey. In this way millions of cinemagoers heard a piece of avant-garde music, performed by an orchestra that devoted itself for years to new music.
artiest/swf-sinfonieorchester-baden-bade.listen: Listen to Atmospheres by Ligeti and notice the dense clouds of sound without a clear beat, in which strings and winds merge into a single moving plane.

artiest/swr-rundfunkorchester-kaiserslau.text:
The SWR Rundfunkorchester Kaiserslautern was a German radio orchestra from Kaiserslautern, attached to the public broadcaster Südwestrundfunk, the broadcaster for the south-west of Germany. That broadcaster came into being on 1 January 1998 from the merger of Südwestfunk in Baden-Baden and Süddeutscher Rundfunk in Stuttgart. The orchestra then came under the SWR and took the name of the broadcaster.

The orchestra is known above all for record recordings of classical repertoire, often with soloists and with lesser-known composers alongside the great names. The list of recordings includes Clarinet Concertos (2005), Complete Piano Concertos (2007), Swedish & Russian Dances (2008) and Violin Concertos 15, 18 & 19 (2009). There was also a release of Peter und der Wolf with excerpts from fairy-tale operas.

Radio orchestras of this kind played an important role in German musical culture: they recorded concerts for the radio, supported soloists and released repertoire that commercial labels often left aside. The recordings of this orchestra sound polished and clear, without great effects, and are valuable above all as documentation of the broad classical tradition.
artiest/swr-rundfunkorchester-kaiserslau.listen: Listen to a recording of Peter und der Wolf and notice how each character has its own instrument, so that you can follow the story by the sound.

artiest/swr-rundfunkorchester-kaiserslau.text:
The SWR Rundfunkorchester Kaiserslautern is a German radio orchestra of the Südwestrundfunk. Frank Strobel is a German conductor who is much involved with film music, especially music for silent films. Together they recorded the music that Dmitri Shostakovich wrote in 1929 for New Babylon, opus 18. That was a Russian silent film about the Paris Commune, made by Grigori Kozintsev and Leonid Trauberg. Shostakovich was then still a very young man, and he wrote the score for the film himself as orchestral music.

The recording belongs to the part of the course that deals with film music. A silent film has no dialogue and no sound effects, so the music has to carry the story, the tension and the pace. Shostakovich used sharp contrasts for this. There are cheerful, almost mocking passages and rougher ones, and that suits the tension between luxury and popular uprising that the film is about.

A performance with an orchestra like this makes the score audible apart from the film. In this way the recording shows that film music is a piece of music history in its own right, even when the film itself is almost forgotten.
artiest/swr-rundfunkorchester-kaiserslau.listen: Listen to the first movement of New Babylon and notice how the music changes mood. Can you hear dance-like, almost mocking passages alongside rougher and more threatening sounds?

artiest/syama-sastri.text:
Syama Sastri was born in 1762 in Tiruvarur, in present-day Tamil Nadu, and died in 1827. He was a composer of Carnatic music, the classical music of South India. His birth name was Venkata Subrahmanya Iyer. He was educated in the Vedas, astrology and other traditional subjects and learned music from his uncle and later from Adiappayya, a well-known court musician from Thanjavur.

Syama Sastri is regarded as the eldest of the Trimurti of Carnatic music, alongside Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar. He composed about three hundred pieces, fewer than his two contemporaries. His works have nevertheless remained well known for their literary, melodic and rhythmic qualities. His texts, mainly addressed to the goddess Kamakshi, are written in a formal Telugu that borrows heavily from Sanskrit. He signed his compositions with the name Syama Krishna. He wrote kritis, varnams and svarajatis. He was probably the first to make svarajatis in such a way that they could be sung or played without dance. His three most famous, Kamakshi Anudinamu, Kamakshi Padayugame and Rave Himagiri Kumari, are together called Ratnatrayam.

His name stands for rhythmic refinement: he was known for his ability to compose in very complex talas. Pupils such as Alasur Krishna Iyer and Porambur Krishna Iyer kept his work alive. For world music he is a key figure from a musical tradition that began long before pop music.
artiest/syama-sastri.listen: Listen to Rave Himagiri Kumari and notice how the melody in raga Todi builds up slowly, with elaborate ornaments in the vocal line.

artiest/syd-barrett.text:
Syd Barrett, born Roger Keith Barrett in Cambridge in 1946, was a singer, guitarist and songwriter. He played in bands from a young age and was friends with Roger Waters, who later became his bandmate. He studied painting in London and in 1965 co-founded the group that called itself Pink Floyd. He came up with that name himself.

Barrett wrote the group's first single, Arnold Layne, about a man who steals clothes from washing lines. See Emily Play followed, and in 1967 the album The Piper at the Gates of Dawn, of which he wrote eight of the eleven songs. He combined English fairy-tale lyrics with a free, experimental way of playing. On guitar he used dissonance, distortion, echo and feedback, and his influence on psychedelic rock was great. Because of serious drug problems and increasingly erratic behaviour, things went wrong in 1968. He left Pink Floyd in April, and David Gilmour took his place.

In 1970 his solo albums The Madcap Laughs and Barrett appeared, recorded with the help of members of Pink Floyd and Soft Machine. In 1974 he stopped making music. He afterwards lived in seclusion, painted and worked in the garden, and died in 2006. Pink Floyd continued to commemorate him, for example with Shine On You Crazy Diamond from 1975. What Barrett revealed in the short time of his career showed others how free a pop song could sound.
artiest/syd-barrett.listen: Listen to Arnold Layne by Pink Floyd. Notice the story about the man who steals clothes, and the way the band turns it into an ordinary pop single with an odd atmosphere.

artiest/sylvain-luc.text:
Sylvain Luc was a French jazz guitarist, born in 1965 in Bayonne, the youngest of three brothers. His brothers played at dances, and he went along with them from a very young age. He also played cello, violin and mandolin. The conservatoire in Bayonne had no guitar lessons, so he chose the cello. That gave him strength in his fingers, he said later. At nine he played on a record by his brothers for the first time. At fifteen he founded the Bulle Quintet, which was a prizewinner at the San Sebastián festival in 1982.

In 1988 he settled in Paris, where he became an arranger, composer and accompanist for, among others, Catherine Lara and Michel Jonasz, and bass player in the trio of Richard Galliano. In 1999 he founded Trio Sud with André Ceccarelli and Jean-Marc Jafet, which in 2003 won a French jazz prize as best group. Later he played in quartets with Didier Lockwood, Victor Bailey and Billy Cobham, and in 2009 he toured with Steve Gadd and Richard Bona. He also collaborated with Al Jarreau, Dee Dee Bridgewater and Michel Legrand. His best-known records are the two duo albums with Biréli Lagrène. He died in 2024.

Luc loved the duet and seldom performed at large festivals. He played virtuosically and melodically, with a great feeling for playing together with another guitarist.
artiest/sylvain-luc.listen: Listen to a duo recording by Sylvain Luc with Biréli Lagrène and notice how the two guitars take over each other's lines, so that at times you can no longer hear who is playing the melody.

artiest/sylvia-robinson.text:
Sylvia Robinson, born Sylvia Vanterpool, was an American singer and producer from Harlem, New York. She was born in 1935, left school at fourteen and recorded from 1950 as Little Sylvia. The guitarist Mickey Baker taught her to play guitar. As the duo Mickey & Sylvia they had a big hit in 1957 with Love Is Strange. After that she also began working behind the scenes. She produced records and played guitar on It's Gonna Work Out Fine by Ike & Tina Turner.

With her husband Joe Robinson she started the soul label All Platinum in New Jersey, where she wrote and produced hits for, among others, The Moments, such as Love on a Two-Way Street. In 1972 she wrote Pillow Talk for Al Green. He did not want to sing it for religious reasons, so she recorded it herself. In 1973 it became a big hit under the name Sylvia: a sultry soul record with sighs and moans, before Donna Summer did the same.

Her greatest influence came with the label Sugar Hill Records. In 1979 she put together The Sugarhill Gang and produced Rapper's Delight, one of the first hip hop records to have commercial success. In 1982 she insisted that Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five record a song about the hard life in the neighbourhood. That is how The Message came about, one of the most influential songs in hip hop. She is therefore sometimes called the mother of hip hop. She died in 2011 and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2022.
artiest/sylvia-robinson.listen: Listen to Pillow Talk from 1973. Notice the relaxed, danceable soul groove and Sylvia's whispering, sighing vocals.

artiest/symarip.text:
Symarip was a British ska and reggae band, founded in the late 1960s by Frank Pitter and Michael Thomas, at that time under the name The Bees. The band members had West Indian roots. The name, at first spelled Simaryp, is roughly a reversal of the word pyramids, one of the group's earlier names. Later they also played as Seven Letters and Zubaba. The line-up included the singer and trombonist Roy Ellis, guitarist Josh Roberts, bass player Mik Thomas, drummer Frank Pitter and keyboard player Monty Neysmith.

Symarip is regarded as one of the first skinhead reggae bands, and one of the first to target skinheads as an audience. Their songs included Skinhead Girl, Skinhead Jamboree and Skinhead Moonstomp, which was based on Moon Hop by Derrick Morgan. The album Skinhead Moonstomp came out in 1970 on Trojan. In 1971 the group moved to Germany, where they played reggae and Afro-rock as Zubaba. In 1980 Skinhead Moonstomp was released again, riding the wave of the 2 Tone craze, and reached number 54 on the British chart. In 1985 the band split up after the album Drunk and Disorderly, released under the name The Pyramids. Later reunions followed.

Symarip belongs to the cradle of skinhead culture, which did not begin with the later rough political imagery, but with a shared love of Jamaican music among Black and white young people. Their sound is danceable, with organ, horns and a light ska beat.
artiest/symarip.listen: Listen to Skinhead Moonstomp and notice the singer's call and the organ above the light ska beat.

artiest/symphonieorchester-des-bayerisch.text:
The Symphonieorchester des Bayerischen Rundfunks is the symphony orchestra of the Bavarian broadcaster, based in Munich. It is one of the four major orchestras of the city. The orchestra was founded in 1949, with members of an earlier radio orchestra as its core. Eugen Jochum was the first chief conductor, until 1960. Rafael Kubelík, Colin Davis, Lorin Maazel and Mariss Jansons followed, the last leading the orchestra from 2003 until his death in 2019. Simon Rattle has taken over that role since the 2023 to 2024 season. The orchestra plays mainly in the Herkulessaal of the Münchner Residenz and in the Philharmonie am Gasteig.

The orchestra is regarded as one of the best in Germany. The core of the repertoire is the symphonic music of the First Viennese School and of Romanticism. Contemporary music also has a permanent place there, partly thanks to the concert series musica viva, which the composer Karl Amadeus Hartmann founded. From the beginning the orchestra played works by Stravinsky and Milhaud, later also by Stockhausen, Kagel, Berio and Eötvös. Recordings have appeared on Deutsche Grammophon, RCA and EMI, among others, and since 2009 on its own label BR-Klassik. In 2006 it won a Grammy for the recording of Shostakovich's thirteenth symphony.

The orchestra shows how a broadcaster can build a sound world of its own, with an orchestra that reaches its audience via radio and record.
artiest/symphonieorchester-des-bayerisch.listen: Listen to Shostakovich's thirteenth symphony by this orchestra under Mariss Jansons and notice the dark chorus of basses and the great dynamic contrasts in the orchestra.

artiest/synaulia.text:
Synaulia is a group of musicians, archaeologists, palaeontologists and choreographers who reconstruct music and dance from antiquity, especially from the Etruscan and Roman periods. The name comes from the ancient Greek word synaulia, which in ancient Rome denoted a group of mainly wind instruments. The group was founded in 1995 by the Italian palaeo-organologist Walter Maioli and the choreographer and anthropologist Natalie Van Ravenstein, at first with the support of the Rijksmuseum van Oudheden (the National Museum of Antiquities) in Leiden.

At first the work was mainly educational: building copies of ancient instruments for the Dutch archaeological centre Archeon. Later the research expanded to the music and dance of Italy, especially of ancient Rome. Because no musical notation from that time has survived, the reconstruction relies on pictorial material, texts, customs and comparative research. The group built wind instruments such as the syrinx, tibiae, cornu and tuba, string instruments such as the lyre, cithara and pandura, and percussion instruments such as the tympanum, cymbal and sistrum. The results were used for films, series and documentaries about ancient Rome, including Gladiator by Ridley Scott and the television series Rome.

Synaulia is not a pop group. The ensemble belongs in an encyclopedia of pop music because it shows how old the making of music with wind, strings and percussion is, and how film music sometimes tries to approximate a lost sound.
artiest/synaulia.listen: Listen to a recording by Synaulia and notice the difference between the wind instruments, the strings and the percussion, and how strange that sound, almost two thousand years old, seems.

artiest/synaulia-walter-maioli.text:
Walter Maioli, born in 1950 in Milan, is an Italian researcher, multi-instrumentalist and composer. He devoted himself to experimental archaeology and to the music of ancient civilisations. In the early 1970s he travelled around the Mediterranean and got to know Arabic, African, Eastern and European music there. In 1972 he founded Aktuala, a pioneer of world music with folkloric music from Africa and Asia. In the 1980s he shifted his attention to prehistoric instruments, and from 1994 he coordinated for a year and a half the music of the archaeological theme park Archeon in Alphen aan den Rijn.

In 1995 he founded Synaulia, a group of musicians, archaeologists, instrument specialists and choreographers. They try to reconstruct ancient Etruscan and Roman music and dance, using copies of instruments from that time. They performed in the Netherlands and Germany and at archaeological sites in Italy, such as Ostia Antica, Villa Adriana and Pompeii. Maioli also provided the reconstructed instruments for the 1998 film A Midsummer Night's Dream.

The music of Synaulia is heard in films and television series. Two tracks were used in Gladiator. The group also worked for Rome by the BBC and HBO and for documentaries by, among others, the BBC and National Geographic. It remains reconstruction: nobody knows exactly how Roman music sounded, but Synaulia lets you hear how it may have sounded.
artiest/synaulia-walter-maioli.listen: Listen to Pompei by Synaulia. Notice which instruments you hear, such as strings, wind instruments and percussion, and how different they sound from a modern pop band.

artiest/system-f.text:
System F is an alias of the Dutch DJ and producer Ferry Corsten, who was born in Rotterdam in 1973. As a teenager he played at school parties and bought his first keyboard with money from washing cars. He made his first records in the 1990s: first hardcore gabber, then club house and trance. He worked under many names, including Moonman, Pulp Victim and Gouryella, and in 1997 founded the dance label Tsunami with Robert Smit.

As System F, Corsten released Out of the Blue in February 1999. The track had been lying around in the clubs as a promo for months and became a worldwide trance hit. The album Out of the Blue, with, among others, Soul on Soul with Marc Almond, followed in 2000. It was the strongest example of Corsten's trance sound: a long-built melody over fast, tight beats, with synthesizers that seem to climb a step higher each time. Together came out later, in 2003. His last System F single, Exhale, he made with Armin van Buuren.

Corsten belongs, together with Tiësto and Armin van Buuren, to the Dutch DJs who made dance music known worldwide. That a Rotterdam producer could make such records in a room in his parents' house shows how strongly Dutch dance grew around the turn of the century.
artiest/system-f.listen: Listen to Out of the Blue and notice the build-up. Can you hear how the melody is repeated again and again and how the tension rises before the beat comes fully back in?

artiest/t-a-t-u.text:
t.A.T.u. is a Russian pop duo consisting of Lena Katina and Julia Volkova. The producer Ivan Shapovalov and his business partner Aleksandr Voitinskiy held auditions for teenage girls in Moscow in 1999. Katina and Volkova, both fourteen, already knew each other and had previously been members of the children's group Neposedy. The name sounds like the English word tattoo and is also an abbreviation of a Russian phrase meaning: this girl loves that girl. The concept made the duo stand out as a romantic couple probing the limits of public debate.

The debut album 200 Po Vstrechnoy (2001) was a success in Eastern Europe. After that the duo signed to Interscope for the English-language version, 200 km/h in the Wrong Lane (2002), with the international hits All the Things She Said and Not Gonna Get Us. It was the first album by a foreign group to reach number one in Japan. In 2003 the duo represented Russia at the Eurovision Song Contest with Ne ver, ne boysya and came third. The second album Dangerous and Moving appeared in 2005 together with the Russian version Lyudi Invalidy. Vesyolye Ulybki and Waste Management followed in 2008 and 2009. In 2011 they split up, but they later reunited several times, including at the opening of the Winter Olympics in Sochi in 2014.

The music is energetic, electronic pop with heavy beats and dramatic choruses. t.A.T.u. showed that Eastern European pop music could also reach the Western charts.
artiest/t-a-t-u.listen: Listen to All the Things She Said and notice how the song starts quietly and bursts out in the chorus, with vocals that swing between vulnerable and desperate.

artiest/t-bone-walker.text:
Aaron Thibeaux Walker, known as T-Bone Walker, was born in 1910 in Linden, Texas, into a musical family. His stepfather taught him guitar, banjo, violin, mandolin and piano, and Blind Lemon Jefferson, a friend of the family, sometimes came to dinner. At fifteen he was a professional musician. In 1929 he made his first record, under the name Oak Cliff T-Bone, with Wichita Falls Blues. In the 1930s he sang in clubs in Los Angeles and played guitar in the orchestra of Les Hite. Around 1940 he began to play electric guitar.

In 1942 he moved to Chicago. His best-known song is Call It Stormy Monday (But Tuesday Is Just as Bad), recorded in 1947 for Black and White Records. Bobby Sox Blues and West Side Baby also did well. From 1950 to 1954 he recorded for Imperial, with Dave Bartholomew. In 1962 he played at the American Folk Blues Festival. In 1970 he won a Grammy for Good Feelin'. He died in 1975, after two strokes.

Walker was a pioneer of jump blues, West Coast blues and electric blues. He played smooth, melodic guitar solos with a soft, jazzy tone, and sang with a warm voice. Many later blues guitarists adopted his approach, and Rolling Stone placed him at number 67 on its list of the greatest guitarists of all time in 2018.
artiest/t-bone-walker.listen: Listen to Call It Stormy Monday (But Tuesday Is Just as Bad) and notice the slow, warm vocals and the short guitar lines that answer between the phrases.

artiest/t-i.text:
T.I., whose real name is Clifford Joseph Harris Jr., is an American rapper and actor. He was born in 1980 and grew up in Atlanta, Georgia. In the late 1990s he joined the label Ghet-O-Vision Entertainment, an imprint of Arista and LaFace Records. His debut album I'm Serious from 2001 disappointed, after which he left the label, signed with Atlantic and in 2003 founded his own label Grand Hustle Records.

The breakthrough came with Trap Muzik in 2003, with the singles Rubber Band Man and Let's Get Away. Urban Legend followed in 2004 and King in 2006, the album with What You Know. That song became a big hit in the United States. With T.I. vs. T.I.P. in 2007 and Paper Trail in 2008 his success grew further. Paper Trail includes Whatever You Like and Live Your Life, with Rihanna. Both reached number one on the American Hot 100.

T.I. is regarded as one of the pioneers of trap, a style from the southern United States with heavy bass, fast hi-hats and stories about street life in Atlanta. The word trap even appears in the title of his second album. His role in the Southern hip hop of the 2000s explains why the course mentions him in the story of the rise of that hip hop.
artiest/t-i.listen: Listen to What You Know and notice the beat and the bass. Can you hear how the producer, with few sounds, leaves a lot of room for T.I.'s voice?

artiest/t-pain.text:
T-Pain is the stage name of Faheem Rashad Najm, an American singer, rapper, songwriter and producer. He was born in 1984 in Tallahassee, Florida. The name stands for Tallahassee Pain, a reference to the difficult time he had there. As a child he already played in a studio belonging to a family acquaintance, and at ten he turned his bedroom into a studio of his own with a keyboard, a drum machine and a four-track recorder. In 1999 he joined the rap group Nappy Headz.

In 2004 he released the mixtape Back @ It. Akon heard an altered version of his song Locked Up and offered him a contract with Konvict Muzik. T-Pain then began to sing instead of rap. In 2005 his first single I'm Sprung was released, followed by the album Rappa Ternt Sanga. The second album, Epiphany from 2007, brought Buy U a Drank to number one in the United States. Thr33 Ringz followed in 2008 and REVOLVE? in 2011. He also sang on other artists' hits, such as Low by Flo Rida and Kiss Kiss by Chris Brown.

T-Pain is known as the man who made the creative use of Auto-Tune a trademark. He used the software with extreme settings, which gave his voice an electronic, almost robotic sound. That combination of singing, rap and R&B determined how much pop music sounded in the 2000s. In this way he showed that a vocal effect can itself become an instrument.
artiest/t-pain.listen: Listen to Buy U a Drank by T-Pain, with Yung Joc. Notice how Auto-Tune makes the voice sound like a synthesizer, and how the melody jumps where an ordinary singing voice would glide.

artiest/t-rex.text:
T. Rex was the English band of the singer, guitarist and songwriter Marc Bolan. He began in 1967 in London with Tyrannosaurus Rex, an acoustic duo with long album titles full of fantasy imagery, such as My People Were Fair and Had Sky in Their Hair… But Now They're Content to Wear Stars on Their Brows (1968). Around 1970 Bolan shortened the name to T. Rex and switched to electric guitar.

Big success came with that. With the albums Electric Warrior (1971) and The Slider (1972) and singles such as Get It On and Metal Guru, T. Rex became one of the most popular groups in England in the early 1970s. Bolan performed in glitter and eye-catching clothes and became one of the faces of glam rock. Later in the 1970s the success declined. Bolan was killed in a car accident in 1977.

The music of T. Rex was simple and direct: short rock songs with a stomping rhythm, boogie guitar and Bolan's soft, quavering voice. That simplicity continued to have an effect. Morrissey and The Smiths used the rhythm of Metal Guru for their song Panic, and the singer Gloria Jones, whose Tainted Love was later covered by Soft Cell, was Bolan's girlfriend.
artiest/t-rex.listen: Listen to Metal Guru and notice the stomping rhythm and the chorus in which the title keeps coming back. Then put it next to Panic by The Smiths: can you hear where Morrissey and Johnny Marr got that rhythm from?
